definition: Applying AI to marketing — content generation, targeting, personalization, and campaign optimization.
details: Applying AI to marketing — content generation, targeting, personalization, and campaign optimization.

explainer.lead: AI marketing uses computer models to help decide what to say, whom to say it to, and how to improve a campaign. It matters because it can speed up content production and make messages more relevant, but the results still depend on good data and clear goals.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a shop helper who remembers what different customers like and suggests something suitable to each person. AI marketing is a computer version of that helper: it can also draft messages and learn which campaign ideas work better. A person still needs to check that its suggestions are useful and fair.
tiers.practitioner: Practitioners use generative models for copy and creative variations, and prediction or recommendation systems for targeting and personalization. Campaign optimization typically connects these outputs to results such as clicks, conversions, or purchases, then tests alternatives against a baseline. Common pitfalls include irrelevant personalization, unreviewed generated content, sparse customer data, and optimizing a short-term metric instead of the actual business goal.
tiers.paperLevel: One useful formulation is to estimate P(y | x, a), where x describes a customer and context, a is a marketing action, and y is an outcome; content generation can separately model p(content | brief). Campaign optimization selects actions or variants using observed outcomes, while personalization ranks messages or offers for each context. Limits include sparse or unrepresentative data, errors in generated content, and disagreement between the optimized metric and long-term customer value.

explainer.example: An online bookshop drafts two email descriptions for a new cookbook. Its system sends the version emphasizing quick meals to customers interested in weeknight cooking and the version emphasizing baking techniques to another relevant group, then compares purchases from the two emails and uses that evidence when planning the next campaign.

explainer.intuition: Marketing involves repeated choices about content, audience, timing, and budget. AI helps by finding patterns in available information, producing candidate messages, and using campaign outcomes to guide the next choices.
howItWorks: Gather the permitted customer, content, and campaign information needed for the task.
Generate content candidates or predict which audiences and messages are likely to be relevant.
Personalize the selected content or offer for each audience or customer context.
Run the campaign and record outcomes such as responses or conversions.
Compare variants and use the results to adjust later content, targeting, or campaign settings.
explainer.whyItMatters: It connects content creation and campaign decisions in one feedback loop, allowing teams to produce more variants and learn from their outcomes. Clear measurement and human review keep speed and personalization from becoming the only goals.
misconceptions: AI marketing is not just text generation; targeting, personalization, and campaign optimization are also central.
Personalization does not guarantee relevance, especially when customer information is sparse or outdated.
A better campaign metric does not automatically prove better long-term customer or business outcomes.
